Side-by-side view displays two columns with line numbers, deletions on the left, insertions on the right, and word-level highlighting on paired changed lines. Unified view shows one column with - lines for deletions, + for insertions, and unchanged lines in between — the format Git emits.

Both unified and side-by-side diff can be augmented with word-level highlighting — showing exactly which words within a modified line changed, rather than just marking the whole line as modified. This is arguably the single highest-impact improvement to diff readability available.

The full line is highlighted because something on it changed, but inside the highlight only the changed tokens carry the bright background (green for added, red strikethrough for removed). This is intra-line word diff: the line context stays readable while your eye lands on the exact edit.

Based on the article's analysis, here are concrete design guidelines:

**Format Selection**
- Side-by-side for refactors with many modifications and complex logic comparisons
- Unified for terminal use, new files, deletion-only changes, and primarily additive updates

**Visual Alignment & Structure**
- Synchronize column scrolling in side-by-side layouts
- Handle blank columns gracefully when one side adds/deletes large blocks
- Maintain spatial alignment between old and new versions for modified lines

**Line-Level Features**
- Display line numbers for reference
- Use context lines to show surrounding unchanged code
- Implement collapsible unchanged sections to reduce cognitive load

**Word-Level Enhancement**
- "Word-level diff works well in unified format and eliminates one of the main advantages" of side-by-side for modified-line review
- Apply word-level highlighting automatically where possible
- Support both color-only and +/- marker variations

**Navigation & Interaction**
- Enable easy toggle between formats (one-click preferred)
- Keyboard shortcuts for navigating between change hunks
- Virtualized rendering for large diffs to maintain performance

- Recognize that "experienced reviewers are more adaptable" across formats
- Match format selection to specific change characteristics rather than forcing one approach universally

content.text:
The file tree now has a small diff button beside every new, untracked or modified file. Clicking it opens that file's diff view beside the task view, where the editor normally goes, and the view switches between side by side and unified. Git awareness is now its own `GitScope`, which the file tree, git panel and diff view all reference. 111 of 113 tests pass: the palette test that was already failing fails, and the real commit-message test is skipped as before. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I haven't looked at the diff view in the running app, so check colours and spacing by eye.

**Design choices, from the research:**
- **Two layouts:**
  - *Side by side:* old on the left, new on the right, each with its own line numbers. A removed line faces the line that replaced it, and a line with no counterpart faces shaded filler so both sides stay level.
  - *Unified:* one column showing both line numbers, with removed lines before the added lines that replaced them.
  - Your choice is remembered, starting side by side.
- **Word-level highlighting:** within a line that changed a little, only the changed words get a stronger tint. The sources call this the biggest single readability win for diffs. A line that changed completely isn't marked word by word.
- **Not colour alone:** added lines are green and marked +, removed lines red and marked −.
- **Collapsed unchanged lines:** like VS Code, 3 lines of context stay either side of each change. Longer unchanged runs collapse into a "Show N unchanged lines" row you click to expand.
- **Moving between changes:** F7 and Shift+F7 (VS Code's keys) or the header arrows. The change you land on is centred and marked with a bar on its left.
- **Header:** file path, "+N −M", the layout switch, "Open file" to switch to the editor, and close.
- **Also:** it follows the file as you edit it, and says so for binary, empty and unreadable files. Rows are virtualized, so large files stay quick.

**What it compares:** the file as of the last commit against the file on disk. A new or untracked file shows entirely as added.

**Tests:**
- Diffing: changed words, pairing lines side by side, collapsing and expanding, new and unchanged files.
- The view on a real repository: the change is found, you can switch to unified, F7 lands on the change, and clicking a collapsed row expands it.
- The tree: a changed file gets a diff button, an unchanged one doesn't, and clicking the button opens the diff without also opening the file.

**Not built yet, from common practice:**
- **Syntax highlighting** inside the diff.
- **Long lines:** there's no horizontal scrolling, so long lines are cut off at the edge.
- **Other options:** an ignore-whitespace toggle, and switching to unified automatically when the view is narrow.
- **Scrolling in step:** side by side, both halves are in one list, so they always scroll together.

**Code:**
- `src/diff.rs` computes the diff, using the `similar` crate I added to `Cargo.toml`.
- `src/diff_view.rs` is the view.
- `src/project_tree.rs` adds the button.
- `src/prompt_mode.rs` shows the diff in the split.

**Spec:**
- **New `GitScope`** (`spec/scope/git/index.pi`): repository detection, statuses and colours, branch and counts, a file's committed version, and refreshing.
- **New `DiffViewScope`** (`spec/ui/components/diff-view/index.pi`): everything above.
- **`FileTreeScope`:** git colouring now refers to `GitScope`, plus a new diff button section.
- **`GitPanelScope`:** takes its branch and counts from `GitScope`.
- **`MainWindow`:** says where the diff opens.

Sources:
- [Side-by-Side vs Unified Diff (DevUtils)](https://utili.dev/blog/side-by-side-vs-unified-diff)
- [Add line+word diff highlighting (openai/codex issue #3090)](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3090)
- [VS Code: Staging and committing changes](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/sourcecontrol/staging-commits)
- [VS Code July 2023 (1.81) release notes](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_81)
- [VS Code Diff Editor v2: options for unchanged regions (#190837)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/190837)
- [VS Code Diff Editor v2: hide unchanged code (#188416)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/188416)
- [Text Diff Viewer, side-by-side + unified](https://diff.tooljo.com/)
- [Understanding Diff Formats (DEV Community)](https://dev.to/shrsv/understanding-diff-formats-a-developers-guide-to-making-sense-of-changes-414o)
